newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore property shares firm but upside limited.
newsitem.headline: Singapore property shares firm but upside limited.

text.p: Singapore property stocks recovered from recent losses following the government's latest loan curbs on public housing and traded higher at mid-morning on Tuesday on a stronger Wall Street.
The property index rose over 10 points to a high of 685.78 before hovering around 680.14 at 0230 GMT, up 5.01 points.
Property heavyweights like City Developments, Cycle & Carriage, DBS Land and Wing Tai were among top gainers and hogged the actives list.
CityDev rose Singapore $0.10 to S$12.20 in active trade of over 2.6 million shares. Cycle & Carriage rose S$0.20 to S$15.00 while DBS Land firmed S$0.10 to S$4.92 on about two million shares.
On Friday, the property index dropped over five percent or 37.84 points to 680.70 ahead of the government's Saturday announcement of tighter loan policies.
Dealers were sceptical the firmer property prices signalled a recovery.
"There is still concern of more curbs on public housing that might impact the private property markets," a dealer said.
"Prices of property counters are up...on Wall Street and some bargain-hunting but buying was very restrained," the dealer said.
The market remains concerned the government is studying more ways to cut the queue of public housing buyers.

The Singapore property market has seen two rounds of curbs so far. The first was in May last year, aimed at speculators in the private housing market and the second, last Saturday, targetted at those who realise capital gains on their public housing.
